t: This is Pentonville Prison, a men's prison on the Caledonian Road. Despite the name, it isn't in Pentonville but further north, in Barnsbury. It is a place with a grim history, because several well known people died here. Hawley Crippen was hanged here for murdering his wife, and was the first criminal caught with the help of wireless telegraphy. Timothy Evans was executed here in 1950 and was later recognised as wrongly convicted. The Irish nationalist Roger Casement died and was buried here, and the Indian revolutionaries Madan Lal Dhingra and Udham Singh also died here.
